Saifee Hospital is a Dawoodi Bohra founded multi-speciality hospital at Charni Road, Mumbai, India, overlooking the Arabian Sea. Saifee Hospital is founded by the head of the Dawoodi Bohra faith, Syedna Mohammad Burhanuddin, dedicated the hospital to the memory of his revered father, Syedna Taher Saifuddin.
History:-
Saifee Hospital was established by the Dawoodi Bohras in 1948 with the aim of providing safe, ethical and affordable medical assistance to people of all faiths and socio-economic backgrounds. In 2000, the foundation of a new hospital on the existing premises was laid down by Dr Syedna Mohammed Burhanuddin. Construction commenced in 2001 and the new hospital was commissioned on 4 June 2005 in the presence of the Prime minister of India, Dr. Manmohan Singh. The architecture of the hospital features a combination of classical Arabian (with domes and arches) and contemporary (with glass curtain facades) styles.
Services:-
The hospital has approximately 257 beds, as well as 44 ICU beds, and 9 operating theaters, and conducts over 10,000 surgeries a year.
Saifee Hospital specializes in bariatric surgeries, cardiology, critical care medicine, dentistry, dermatology, gynecology, hepatology, oncology, neurology, nephrology, ophthalmology, neonatology, high dose radioactive therapy units, and Pressurized Intra Peritoneal Aerosol Chemotherapy (PIPAC). The hospital features a highly advanced Robotic Surgical System to facilitate the surgeon in performing complex but minimally invasive surgery.
In the aftermath of the 2011 Mumbai bombings, Saifee Hospital provided free treatment to victims and others affected by the bomb blast.

I am.  Sumit Gupta  from Varanasi. I was diagnosed with Stage 3 cancer in 2018 and took my treatment at Wadia Hospital. Today, I am a proud cancer survivor.
My experience in the Hemato-Oncology department was really wonderful. During my treatment, all the doctors, nurses, and staff supported me a lot. Dr. Sangeeta Ma'am is very kind and caring. She treats every child like her own and always makes patients feel comfortable. I am also thankful to Dr. Apurva, Dr. Ritika, and all the other doctors who were always polite, gentle, and supportive.
The nurses worked very hard and took great care of us. The mamas in the ward were also very caring and loving. They always helped the children and kept the department clean and comfortable.
The dietitians and counselors helped me a lot during my treatment. They guided me and supported me whenever I needed help. The NGO members were also very understanding and supportive throughout my journey.
One of my favorite memories is the play area and the small school run by CanKids for cancer patients. During chemotherapy, I spent time there learning, playing, and enjoying myself. The teachers in the school were also very kind, polite, and caring. They always encouraged us to learn and kept us motivated even during difficult times. Their support made a big difference in my journey and helped me stay positive.
What made Wadia Hospital special for me was that it never felt like a hospital. It felt like a second home because of the caring environment and the people around me. Even today, if I have any health-related concerns, I still visit Wadia Hospital because I trust the doctors and staff completely.
I will always be grateful to everyone at Wadia Hospital for helping me through one of the toughest phases of my life and giving me the strength to move forward. Wadia Hospital will always have a special place in my heart

featured_reviews.name: Subhash Chandra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Very Disappointing & Inhumane Experience

My family had a deeply distressing experience at Wadia Children’s Hospital.

My newborn nephew (8 days old, delivered via C-section) was transferred here from Fatima Hospital, Malad. After the transfer, what we expected to be advanced care turned into a nightmare for the mother.

Despite being only 8 days post C-section, my sister Kanchan was told she must stay 24 hours continuously to prepare formula milk, feed the baby, and change diapers. There was no adequate support from nursing staff or ayas, even though these services are part of hospital care.

Shockingly, the hospital did not provide a proper place to rest or sleep for a post-operative mother. When she requested help from nurses, she was spoken to rudely and yelled at, being told “don’t ask me”. This behavior is unacceptable in any medical institution, especially one caring for newborns and recovering mothers.

To make matters worse, her husband was also required to remain in the hospital 24 hours, preventing him from working—the only earning member—while still being expected to bear the high hospital expenses.

Despite repeated requests, no real assistance or empathy was shown. This experience reflects poor patient care, lack of humanity, and extremely unprofessional staff behavior.

I sincerely hope hospital management and trustees take this seriously and improve policies, staff training, and basic compassion toward parents in vulnerable situations.

I would strongly advise parents to carefully evaluate before choosing this hospital.

So I will never recommend this hospital & doctor for any planned treatment. Ours was an emergency so we were stuck.
